items.title: ICC finally recognises Nepal Premier League
items.desc: The International Cricket Council sanctions the third edition of the tournament, which is scheduled to run from October 26 to November 21.

items.title: Nepal to Host ICC Asia Conference in November
items.desc: High-ranking international cricket delegates and representatives from Test and Associate nations will gather in Kathmandu, with visitors slated to watch the NPL playoffs.

items.title: How Rabindra Shakya is keeping the art of repoussé alive
items.desc: Shakya has spent more than 35 years practising repoussé, a centuries-old craft that can take nearly two years to complete a single large piece.

items.title: UML pulls out of Madhesh provincial government
items.desc: The party withdrew its support, accusing the Nepali Congress-led coalition of failing to implement a 15-point agreement, leaving the government in a minority.

items.title: 30MW Khani Khola hydropower project begins test generation
items.desc: The project in Dolakha district is supplying electricity to the national grid during a 15-day testing period before commercial operations begin.

items.title: Government declares flood- and landslide-hit areas in three districts disaster zones
items.desc: The three-month designation covers six local units or parts of them in Gorkha, Dhading and Baglung, with affected families eligible for monthly housing and livelihood assistance of at least Rs15,000.

items.title: Modi’s predicament: Gen Z pours out on India’s streets as dissent surges
items.desc: Youth-led protests over alleged voter-roll manipulation have tapped into wider anger over unemployment, exam leaks and divisive politics, posing the biggest challenge to Modi since he came to power in 2014.

items.title: Dashain shopping picks up, but livestock sales lag in Chitwan
items.desc: Traders who brought goats and Himalayan goats from western Nepal had hoped for brisk business, but buyers have been slower to arrive than expected.

items.title: Congress convention vote count concludes
items.desc: Counting for all 229 positions in the Nepali Congress’s 15th general convention ended on Friday morning, taking a week compared with 12 days at the previous convention.

items.title: US Secretary of State to skip New Delhi for Jamnagar, Mumbai
items.desc: This visit comes as US oligarch Elon Musk described Mukesh Ambani as the “real boss of India” last week.

items.title: Nepal should be a ‘strategic broker’, not a buffer, says Amitabh Mattoo
items.desc: The JNU professor says diplomacy, stronger institutions and regional engagement can help Nepal play a greater role as Asia’s power balance shifts.

items.title: Pāyāḥ was once a tribute to Ajimā. What does the ritual mean today?
items.desc: The procession, rooted in Newa beliefs and traditions, has evolved in ways that threaten to overshadow its original significance.

items.title: BYD after-sales chiefs outline plans for EV ecosystem in Nepal
items.desc: The Chinese EV maker says it will expand service capacity, improve spare parts availability, and train technicians as sales grow in Nepal.

items.title: Attorney General opens settlement route in cases where organised-crime charges fail
items.desc: A new circular allows settlements in certain criminal cases once a court rejects a linked organised-crime charge and the appeal process ends. Former judges warn the provision could be misused.

items.title: Credit picks up, but Nepal’s banks are awash with cash
items.desc: Bankers say rising import costs, festive demand and currency depreciation, not a broad-based economic recovery, are driving much of the increase.

items.title: Build infrastructure that stands the test of time
items.desc: From now on, disaster resilience must guide every stage of Nepal’s reconstruction.

items.title: Is your local police station ready for the internet?
items.desc: Crime now arrives as a friend request, a familiar voice, a link too good to ignore. Policing it will take better machines, better-prepared personnel and a public that trusts us enough to talk.

items.title: Are we training our daughters to be unpaid workers?
items.desc: Nepal pays billions a year for work it does not count and daughters it did not educate.

items.title: Rejection of two ambassadorial nominees brings RSP tensions into focus
items.desc: The committee’s decision raises questions about the government’s vetting process and its promise to prioritise merit over political connections.

items.title: Nepal’s Asian Games star Sherpa criticises government for reward disparity
items.desc: Sherpa, a bronze medallist in the 20th Asian Games, voices deep disappointment over state reward rules while urging authorities to value the sweat and sacrifice of the athletes.

items.title: Can AI fake a Nepali voice convincingly? Here’s what the experts say
items.desc: As Nepalis debate the authenticity of viral recordings allegedly featuring a sitting lawmaker, experts explain how convincingly AI can mimic Nepali speech and how forensic analysis can verify the audio.

items.title: Janakraj Sapkota’s new novel brings Madhesh’s caste oppression to the fore
items.desc: ‘Magani Marik’ follows a character from the Dom community, among the most marginalised in Nepal’s caste hierarchy, and explores the discrimination and hardship shaping everyday life.

items.title: How will Nepal verify those missing after the Bhotekoshi floods?
items.desc: The government has begun compiling an official list of people missing in the August 26 disaster. The process will determine who can be declared dead and whose families qualify for relief.

items.title: Nepal bans 47 immunosuppressant brands, doctors question move
items.desc: Department of Drug Administration has cited safety concerns but doctors say the move could disrupt supplies of life-saving medicines for transplant patients.

items.title: More than 1,200 farm animals lost in Budhigandaki floods
items.desc: The disaster also destroyed 34 livestock sheds and 12 pig pens, while veterinary teams treat rescued animals and deliver feed and medicines to affected areas.

items.title: Nepal arrests four medical service providers as Malaysia recruitment row deepens
items.desc: Police accuse them of collecting an unauthorised biomedical fee from migrant workers, while labour ministry officials say a bilateral technical committee had approved the charge. The foreign ministry had urged a diplomatic solution.

items.title: At least 33 killed, including 32 students, in Pakistan school roof collapse
items.desc: The collapse at a school in Peshawar killed 32 children aged seven to 14 and a female teacher, prompting calls for a probe and safety audits of educational institutions across Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.
